description: Bounded stack bookkeeping atoms — push / pop / peek / is_empty — proven against the len <= cap invariant using Z3 integer theory. Mirrors std/container/safe_queue.mm but with LIFO semantics. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/container/stack — verified bounded stack'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/container/safe_queue.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only what std/core.mm and std/container/safe_queue.mm already use (checked_add, checked_sub, conditional expressions).

atoms.name: stack_push
atoms.description: Push a new element onto a bounded stack. Requires len < cap so the invariant len <= cap is preserved. Returns len + 1.

atoms.name: stack_pop
atoms.description: Pop the top element from a bounded stack. Requires len > 0 so the resulting len stays >= 0. Returns len - 1.

atoms.name: stack_peek
atoms.description: Index of the top element. Requires len > 0; returns len - 1 which is in [0, cap). Pure bookkeeping; no array theory.

atoms.name: stack_is_empty
atoms.description: Predicate: returns 1 when the stack is empty (len == 0), 0 otherwise. The contract pins the boolean encoding to {0, 1}.
